messages:
maria: Noticed a p99 spike (~+11%) for Flash variants after last runtime deploy, surfaced by nightly bench.
jon: Paste the bench output?
maria: Nightly harness summary (main vs canary):
```
model  seq  batch  p99_main  p99_canary  delta
gpt-j  1024   4   48.2 ms   54.1 ms     +12.2%
gpt-j   512   8   24.8 ms   27.7 ms     +11.7%
gpt-neo 256  16   13.4 ms   14.6 ms     +8.9%
```
akshay: Did kernel selector change? fused_flash vs paged_flash?
maria: I dumped selector logs for gpt-j/1024:
```
[selector] model=gpt-j seq=1024 batch=4 -> selected_kernel=paged_flash
reason: kv_coldness_score=0.62 (threshold=0.6) -> prefer paged
```
On main it selected fused_flash.
perf-bot: nightly-harness run 1939999799 alert: flash_variant p99 +12.2% -> #eng-runtime
sara: Any KV cache changes in the deploy?
jon: Commit abc1234 (2026-03-15) adjusted prefetch scoring and introduced batching_coalesce optimization to coalesce short requests. Could affect KV locality and selector inputs.
maria: I forced kernels on the canary host to compare:
```
./bench_tool --model gpt-j --seq 1024 --batch 4 --force-kernel=fused_flash --runs=6
./bench_tool --model gpt-j --seq 1024 --batch 4 --force-kernel=paged_flash --runs=6
```
Results:
- forced fused_flash: p99 = 48.5 ms
- forced paged_flash: p99 = 55.0 ms
So paged_flash is notably slower.
akshay: Selector flipped because kv_coldness_score believed cache was colder. Any KV hit metrics?
maria: Trace shows hit rate drop on canary vs main for same workload:
```
main: hits=8432 misses=1024 hit_rate=89.2%
canary: hits=7801 misses=2055 hit_rate=79.1%
```
jon: That explains the selector decision. Why did hit rate fall? The batching_coalesce change might group requests with different prefixes, reducing prefix locality.
maria: I ran repro toggling the coalesce flag:
- coalesce=on -> hit_rate=79% -> paged_flash selected
- coalesce=off -> hit_rate=90% -> fused_flash selected
sara: So the batching heuristic indirectly regressed latency by hurting KV locality and triggering a different kernel.

maria: Proposed remediation:
1) Flip batching_coalesce off on canary immediately (quick rollback flag).
2) Add selector hysteresis: require 2 successive low-hit windows before switching to paged_flash.
3) Add nightly canary smoke that asserts p99 within 5% for seq=512/1024 mixed-prefix workloads.

jon: I'll implement the hysteresis PR and unit + integration tests. I'll document the batcher->kv-locality->selector interaction in code comments.
sara: I toggled the flag on canary now.
devops: done — batching_coalesce disabled on canary group canary-2. Watchdog will report in 10m.
maria: Re-ran bench after toggle: p99 ~48.9 ms, kv hit_rate back to 90.1%.
perf-bot: Created issue perf-issue/RT-398 with logs and bench artifacts.
jon: I'll open the PR and add a synthetic test exercising coalesce path with cached prefixes.
sara: Also adding an exporter metric for kv_coldness_score per route for alerting and dashboards.
maria: Filing the ticket with reproduction steps and linking artifacts; assigning @jon for selector changes.
jon: Will include a short perf test and a canary gate in the PR.

maria: Thanks all. Closing thread unless anyone has other ideas. :thumbsup:
jon: LGTM
sara: Good catch!
